description: Backend API for RentNest, a property rental platform with Tenant, Landlord, and Admin roles.
notes: There is NO global versioned prefix like /api/v1 - the base path is just /api.
Auth is JWT-based via cookies (accessToken, refreshToken) OR an 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' header.
Login sets httpOnly cookies AND returns the tokens in the JSON body, so a frontend can use either cookie-based or header-based auth.
There is NO runtime request-body validation library (no zod/joi) - only TypeScript interfaces at compile time on the backend. The frontend should still validate inputs before sending.

IMPORTANT BACKEND BUG: almost all errors are returned as HTTP status 500, with a hardcoded message 'failed to register user' regardless of the actual error (e.g. not-found, forbidden, duplicate, bad login). The REAL reason is in the 'error' field of the error response body. The frontend should display response.error (or response.message) rather than relying on the HTTP status code to distinguish error types.
Response success envelope shape is inconsistent across endpoints - some return 'data' as a raw array/object, others wrap lists as 'data.result'. This is called out per-endpoint below.
'price' (Properties) and 'amount' (Payments) are stored as STRING in the database, not numbers - the frontend should parseFloat/Number() them for display and calculations.
No pagination is implemented anywhere, even though the response envelope has an optional 'meta' field for it.
No PUT/PATCH/DELETE routes exist for Reviews, and there is no GET-reviews-by-property endpoint at all.
No logout endpoint and no refresh-token endpoint exist, despite a refreshToken being issued at login.
GET /properties/:id does NOT include the 'category' relation, unlike GET /properties which does - likely a backend oversight.

deliveryMethods: httpOnly cookie 'refreshToken' (set automatically by POST /auth/login, not currently used by any endpoint)
Authorization header, either 'Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>' or raw 'Authorization: <accessToken>'
